reason: Both cover adrenal corticosteroid synthesis, sex-steroid synthesis, steroidogenic regulation and secretion, the wider CYP and vitamin D/retinoid disease family and endocrine-hormone contexts, but A repeats the CYP11B/21/17 steroidogenesis core across many near-identical themes while B gives the same facets with far less redundancy.

A covers catecholamine catabolism, serotonin metabolism, organic-cation/choline clearance, BH4-linked catecholamine synthesis, sympathoadrenal development, monoamine reuptake, dopaminergic signalling/behaviour and broad neurotransmission in about ten distinct themes, whereas B adds little beyond a clean catecholamine-synthesis theme and is cluttered with many overlapping transporter/uptake variants.

A lays out the transporter contexts (bile/ABCB11 cholestasis, drug resistance, organic cation, organic anion/SLCO drug ADME, nucleoside drugs, bilirubin conjugation-excretion, bile acid homeostasis, phase I/II xenobiotic metabolism) once each, while B covers the same ground plus a small environmental-chemical response theme but buries it under a dozen near-duplicate SLCO/ADME/bilirubin variants.

B keeps the meaningful contexts (aminoacylation core, t6A/wobble fidelity modifications, diphthamide/wybutosine, selenocysteine/readthrough, tRNA processing, mitochondrial translation and gene expression) with modest redundancy, whereas A has roughly 40 themes with heavy near-duplication and off-target groupings (creatine, arylsulfatase, polyamines, OXPHOS assembly), only partly offset by its translation-initiation and ribosome quality-control themes.

Both share the same placental core (labyrinth branching, chorio-allantoic fusion, giant cells, decidualization, trophectoderm) plus mammary and gonadal/reproductive-endocrine contexts, but A adds loosely related germline/piRNA/MZT, fertilization and diffuse organ-branching themes and duplicate gonad themes that clutter rather than inform about chorionic trophoblast differentiation.

Both present the same facets (megakaryocyte/platelet programme, RUNX-family transcriptional regulation, erythroid-megakaryocytic commitment, myeloid progenitor/granulopoiesis, HSC regulation, broad haematopoiesis), but A has more near-duplicate themes repeating the same Mk-erythroid and RUNX1 sets, so B is somewhat less cluttered for equal coverage.
